entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:7, the angel says the disciples will see Jesus in Jerusalem.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Observe the message the angel sends to the disciples.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The meeting is set in Galilee, where the disciples will see him, as he had told them.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of Matthew 28:7: Jesus is going ahead of them to Galilee.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look for the place the angel mentions.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:5, tap who the angel is speaking to.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Identify who receives the first announcement of the resurrection.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The angel speaks to the women: they are the first to hear the news.

feedbackWrong.a: "Jesus" is the one they are looking for; the angel speaks to those who came to the tomb.
feedbackWrong.c: "anjo" (angel) is the one speaking, not the one listening.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: See who the angel turns to.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: According to Matthew 28:6, what does the angel invite the women to do?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Observe the angel's invitation at the empty tomb.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The angel calls them to see the empty place with their own eyes.

feedbackWrong.a: There's no body to prepare: Jesus has already risen.
feedbackWrong.b: The guards don't even appear in the angel's words; he calls the women to see.
feedbackWrong.d: The angel doesn't ask them to wait: he says Jesus is not there.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Read the last sentence of the verse.

options.b: Call the guards of the tomb
options.c: See the place where he lay
options.d: Wait there until Jesus comes back

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: Put Matthew 28:2 in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: That's the verse's sequence: the earthquake, the angel coming down, and the stone rolled away.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse starts with the earthquake and ends with the angel sitting on the stone.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: The verse starts with something that shakes the earth.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:8, with what feelings do the women leave the tomb?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Remember how the women react to the announcement.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: Fear and great joy together: the news frightens them and, at the same time, fills them with life.

feedbackWrong.a: "Dúvida" (doubt) doesn't fit: they don't stand there doubting; they run to tell the news.
feedbackWrong.c: "Tristeza" (sadness) doesn't fit: they came to the tomb to mourn, but leave with something else in their hearts.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Next to the fear there is an opposite feeling.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.question: What does Matthew 28:6 communicate that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Connect Matthew 28:6 to the women's surprise at the tomb.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: They were looking for a body, and the angel announces: he is not here, because he has risen.

feedbackWrong.a: The angel calls them to see the place where he lay: it's the right tomb.
feedbackWrong.c: The angel doesn't speak of theft: he says he has risen.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look at the reason the angel gives for the empty tomb.

options.a: They went to the wrong tomb
options.b: He has risen and is not there

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:5–6, the women need not be afraid because the guards had already fled.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Understand the reason behind "Não tenham medo".
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The reason is different: Jesus, whom they seek, is not there because he has already risen.

feedbackWrong.true: The angel doesn't mention the guards; the reason comes after the "pois": Jesus has already risen.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look for the reason the angel himself gives.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:6, tap the word that introduces the reason Jesus is not there.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in the angel's announcement.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" opens the explanation: he is not there because he has already risen.

feedbackWrong.a: "Como" links the resurrection to what Jesus had said; it doesn't give the reason.
feedbackWrong.c: "Onde" points to the place where he lay, not to the reason.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look for the word that comes right after "Não está aqui".

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:6, what does the phrase "como ele havia dito" show about the resurrection?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Relate the resurrection to Jesus' earlier word.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The resurrection is no improvisation: Jesus had said it would happen, and it did.

feedbackWrong.a: The phrase is about Jesus' word, not about who believed.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus had announced it beforehand; nothing caught him by surprise.
feedbackWrong.c: The one announcing is the angel, recalling Jesus' word, not the women.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Think about who had said it and what had been said.

options.a: It only counts for those who already believed
options.b: It took even Jesus by surprise
options.c: It was the women's idea at the tomb
options.d: It fulfills what Jesus himself had announced

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: How does the scene move forward in Matthew 28:8–9?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the tomb to the meeting with Jesus.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: They leave, run to tell the news and, on the way, Jesus himself meets them.

feedbackWrong.default: The meeting with Jesus comes last, when they are already on their way to the disciples.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: The end point is the meeting.

options.a: They leave the tomb in a hurry
options.b: They run to tell the disciples
options.c: Jesus meets them on the way

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:7, what does the angel say Jesus is doing in relation to the disciples?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Understand what the risen Jesus does for his own.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The living Jesus goes on ahead: he is already waiting for his own in Galilee.

feedbackWrong.b: "Atrás" (behind) doesn't fit: Jesus doesn't come later; he gets to Galilee first.
feedbackWrong.c: "Longe" (far away) doesn't fit: he doesn't distance himself; he sets a meeting with them.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Think about who gets to Galilee first.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.question: What connects Matthew 28:6 to Matthew 16:21?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Relate the empty tomb to the announcement Jesus made.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: In 16:21 Jesus says he would die and rise; in 28:6 the angel recalls: "como ele havia dito".

feedbackWrong.a: The one who announces it is Jesus; the women go to the tomb expecting to find a body.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus doesn't speak of escaping: he says he would be killed and rise again.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Compare the end of the two verses.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: Matthew 28:5–6 treats the resurrection as a fact that can be checked, not just as a living memory of Jesus.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Interpret the resurrection as a real event, not just a symbolic one.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The angel points to an empty place and invites the women to see with their own eyes.

feedbackWrong.false: The angel doesn't speak of a memory: he calls the women to see the place where the body lay.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look at the invitation that closes verse 6.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:9, tap the gesture that shows the risen Jesus has a real body.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Support from the text that the resurrection is bodily.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: They hold his feet: not a vision or a memory, but Jesus alive, with a body.

feedbackWrong.b: "Aproximando-se" (coming near): they approach, but the gesture that shows the body comes right after.
feedbackWrong.c: "Saudações" is Jesus' greeting; it shows he speaks, not that he can be touched.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Look for what the women touch.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: What reading does Matthew 28:5–6 support about the resurrection?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about the resurrection.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: The text joins both ends: the one who was crucified is the one who rose, as he had said.

feedbackWrong.a: The angel speaks of "Jesus, que foi crucificado": the death was real.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus had already announced it, and the women are sent out because of it.
feedbackWrong.d: The angel doesn't speak of memory: he shows the empty place where the body lay.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Compare each option with what the angel says about Jesus in the two verses.

options.a: Jesus only fainted and then recovered
options.b: Jesus truly died and came back to life, as he said
options.c: It's just a detail at the end of Jesus' story
options.d: The memory of Jesus lived on among his followers

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: Which sequence shows the place of Matthew 28:6 in the Bible's story?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: See the resurrection as the center of the biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: Death enters at the fall, is defeated at the resurrection, and vanishes in the new creation.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: fall (Gen 3:19), resurrection (Matt 28:6) and new creation (Rev 21:4).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: Follow the Bible's order: beginning, center and end.

options.a: With the fall, death enters the story
options.c: In the new creation, there will be no more death

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: In Matthew 28:6, what word explains why Jesus is not there?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: He didn't leave the tomb like someone who walks away: he came back from death to life.

feedbackWrong.a: "Partiu" (left) would only say he went away; the angel says he defeated death.
feedbackWrong.c: "Fugiu" (fled) doesn't fit: no one escapes from a tomb; the angel announces new life, not an escape.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: It's the word that gives the scene its name.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.question: What connects Matthew 28:6 to 1 Corinthians 15:21–22?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.learningObjective: Connect Jesus' resurrection to the death that entered at the fall.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.feedbackCorrect: Death came through a man; Jesus' resurrection opens life to all who are in him.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul says more: in Christ, all will be made alive.
feedbackWrong.c: It's not a return to the old life: it's victory over the death that came with Adam.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-06-.hint: See whom Paul puts on each side: one brings death, the other life.

options.a: Only Jesus comes back to life
options.b: In Adam death, in Christ life
options.c: A return to the old life

estudo:entrada-biblia-06.context: Jesus had been crucified and buried, and a large stone sealed the tomb, watched by guards. On the first day of the week, some women go there. They expect to find a body.
estudo:entrada-biblia-06.focusQuestion: What changes in your fear of death if Jesus' tomb is empty?
estudo:entrada-biblia-06.keywordGloss: Jesus comes back from death to life, as he had said, and the tomb is left empty.
facts: An angel of the Lord rolled away the stone from the entrance.
The guards trembled and became like dead men.
The angel tells the women not to be afraid.
Jesus is not in the tomb: he has risen, as he had said.
The women are sent to tell the disciples.
Jesus meets the women on the way.
